subject: Performance SLO / VPC qualification - network path & latency follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Barnes <chris.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLO / VPC qualification - next steps

Hi Chris / Priya,

Thanks again for the time this morning - good call. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned on ACME's latency/throughput expectations for the private/VPC deployment: 

Summary of requirements from the call:
- Target tail latency (p95) for normal inference: <= 120ms at typical request sizes (~1k tokens).
- Peak concurrency target: 300 concurrent sessions with sustained bursts to 600 for 2-5 minutes.
- Streaming requirements: average small-chunk RTT target <= 80ms to preserve interactivity.
- Throughput: ~120k tokens/minute steady-state, with 250k tokens/minute burst capacity.
- Network: plan is VPC peering with egress to Redwood edge in us-west-2; you mentioned internal latency budget of 40ms between your app tier and the peered subnet.

Ask / next steps: 
1) Can your networking team provide a recent traceroute/tracert and a sample tcpdump or pcap from the app tier to the peering IP (ideally during a representative load window)? (attachment: network-trace-20270424.pcap)
2) Confirm whether ACME will set up a static route for Redwood's edge IPs vs. using a transit gateway/NAT (any constraints on egress IPs?).
3) Share your expected sustained request size distribution (tokens per request) and percentage of streaming vs non-streaming calls.
4) We'll run an abbreviated test plan once we have network captures - propose Wed 2027-04-28 10:00 PT for a short network/latency test (20-30min).

I've attached a preliminary SLO matrix (slo-matrix-acme-20270425.xlsx) that maps our runtime profiles to your targets and shows proposed fallback policies if tail latency exceeds thresholds. Jordan / Aditya - please see the highlighted network checks we discussed.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172
redwood.ai

Attachments: network-trace-20270424.pcap, slo-matrix-acme-20270425.xlsx
From: Chris Barnes <chris.barnes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, ACME Networking <networks@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO / VPC qualification - next steps

Thanks Marissa - great summary. A few quick answers from our side and I've looped in the networking team.

1) Attached a sample pcap from last week's load test (we'll add the specific peering IP flows for you). We'll also run a fresh capture during the maintenance window today and share.
2) We're planning to use a transit gateway for now; we can add a static route if Redwood prefers. Egress IPs are currently NATed; we can reserve and share a small set of static egress IPs if needed for firewall rules.
3) Request size distribution: ~70% short interactive (~600-1,200 tokens), 30% longer batch (1,500-3,000 tokens). Streaming is about ~45% of interactive calls.
4) Wed 2027-04-28 10:00 PT works for a short run - Priya, can you confirm with networking?

Notes from networking (ACME Networking): we've seen ~25-35ms median internal hop latency between app tier and peered subnets; occasional spikes to ~60ms during maintenance windows. We'll provide traceroutes and a second pcap by EOD.

Chris

--
Chris Barnes
Head of Applied AI, ACME Corp
chris.barnes@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0100
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Chris Barnes <chris.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: ACME Networking <networks@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-25T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO / VPC qualification - next steps

Marissa,

Confirming networking will run a fresh capture and traceroute this afternoon and share the outputs (including timestamps) - we'll include sample flows that match your token distributions. Also confirming transit gateway setup but we can stand up static routes to Redwood edge IPs if that reduces variability.

One thing to flag: our security team requires that any sustained peering endpoints are registered with our change control and that we exchange a signed network diagram + IP list before go-live. I'll attach the network contact and change-control template after the capture.

Priya

--
Priya Singh
Product Manager, ACME Corp
priya.singgh@acme.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Chris Barnes <chris.barnes@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLO / VPC qualification - next steps

Thanks for the updates all. Quick internal note on action items from our side: 

- Aditya: will prepare a short test harness to run a streaming RTT test and a short concurrency burst (approx 600 sessions) against ACME's peering endpoint - this will be instrumented to capture p95/p99 and chunk RTT.
- Marissa: please share the exact peering IPs and the traceroutes when ACME sends them so we can pin the test targets.
- I'll prepare a lightweight runbook for the Wed 4/28 test (20-30min) including rollback steps and data capture points.

Attached: slo-matrix-acme-20270425.xlsx (updated with recommended runtime profiles and fallback thresholds).

Jordan
